questions.question: Which keyword is used to define a function in Python?
questions.explanation: The teaching material states that a function is defined with the def keyword.

questions.question: What is the difference between parameters and arguments in a Python function?

options.A: Parameters are values supplied in a call, arguments are names in the definition
options.B: Parameters are names for values in the definition, arguments are values supplied in a call
options.C: Both terms refer to the names of variables inside the function body
options.D: Both terms refer to the values passed when calling the function

questions.explanation: The material specifies that parameters are names for values in a definition, while arguments are the values supplied during a call.

questions.question: What does Python return if a function reaches the end of its body without executing a return statement?
questions.explanation: According to the text, if a function ends without a return statement, Python returns None.

questions.question: Where can a variable assigned inside a function be read normally?

options.C: Only inside the function unless declared global
options.D: Only if it is passed as an argument

questions.explanation: The material states that variables assigned inside a function are local to that function unless declared global.

questions.question: What rule must be followed regarding the order of parameters with default values in a function definition?

options.A: They must come before parameters without default values
options.B: They can be placed in any position
options.C: They must come after parameters without default values
options.D: They cannot be used in the same function

questions.explanation: The teaching material specifies that parameters with default values must come after parameters without default values.
